subject: Request for records of processing, subprocessor map, and DPIA evidence
summary: Zephyr Health procurement team requested Records of Processing (RoPA/Art.30), an up-to-date subprocessor map (Art.28), DPIA support materials, and SOC2 evidence. Internal legal and security coordinated delivery of exports, redlined DPA, and report links; proposed short call and clarified audit scope.
messages:
From: Maria Lucas <maria.lucas@zephyrhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: records of processing & DPIA supporting evidence

Hi Karthik,

We're moving through Zephyr's procurement privacy review and need a few items to close our assessment by next week (target: 2026-03-10):

- A machine-readable export or RoPA (Records of Processing / Art.30) showing processing activities for the services you provide to us (data categories, purposes, retention).
- Current subprocessor list (Art.28) with regions and whether SCCs/DPF apply.
- Any DPIA / dataflow diagrams or a DPIA support pack you can share — Zephyr will use this to confirm residual risk for our clinical data workload.
- Copy of your latest SOC 2 Type II or a summary report and confirmation of audit access (remote evidence or auditor engagement).

Can you confirm what you can provide and a realistic timeline? Also flag any restrictions on sharing (redactions or NDAs needed).

Thanks — appreciate a quick reply so we can plan the security review.

Regards,
Maria Lucas
Senior Procurement Manager
Zephyr Health
maria.lucas@zephyrhealth.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Lucas <maria.lucas@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-03T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: records of processing & DPIA supporting evidence

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Monica (Security) so we can assemble the right artifacts.

Quick answers and a proposed next step:
- We can provide a RoPA export (xlsx) and an up-to-date subprocessors CSV.
- We maintain standard contractual protections (2021 SCCs) for EU transfers; for US transfers we can confirm mechanism per account (SCCs or DPF where applicable).
- DPIA: Customers typically lead the DPIA, but we can provide a vendor DPIA pack (dataflow diagram, processing descriptions, control mapping) and template language you can use in your assessment.
- SOC2 Type II: we can share a summary and coordinate an auditor request for remote evidence; on-site audits are possible but scheduled and limited.

Can you confirm whether Zephyr needs the full RoPA for all customers or just the processing activities specific to Zephyr's account? Also propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm scope; pls pick a time and I'll set up the meeting.

I'll follow up with the artifacts in a separate email from Legal/Security once we confirm scope.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0199

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Maria Lucas <maria.lucas@zephyrhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-03T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: records of processing & DPIA supporting evidence

Hi Maria — Laura from Legal here. Thanks for the procurement checklist — we've reviewed and can deliver the items you listed with the following clarifications and constraints: 

1) RoPA / Art.30 export: we'll provide an account-scoped RoPA spreadsheet (RoPA-export-2026.xlsx) that lists processing activities specific to Zephyr's use of the Redwood platform (data categories, legal basis, retention periods, subprocessors involved). We do not disclose other customers' data.

2) Subprocessors (Art.28): attached is the current subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_2026.csv) including region and whether SCCs are in effect. Note: subprocessors with operations in APAC are identified and flagged in the CSV.

3) DPA and Audit Rights: attached is a redlined DPA (redlined_DPA_v3.pdf) that highlights where audit rights are scoped to remote evidence and auditor questionnaires. Our standard DPA provides for: remote evidence review, auditor access to relevant logs and controls via secure channels, and mutually agreed on-site audits subject to scheduling and limited scope (to protect multitenant infrastructure). If Zephyr requires extended on-site audit rights, we can discuss a bespoke contractual appendix.

4) DPIA support: Redwood can provide a vendor DPIA pack (dataflow diagram, control mapping to our security program, and suggested language for your DPIA). We are not able to perform Zephyr's DPIA but will support it with these materials and a short technical session if helpful.

5) SOC 2: Monica will share SOC2 evidence and the process for remote auditor requests.

Planned deliverables & timeline: RoPA/export + subprocessors CSV + redlined DPA + SOC2 summary by end of day 2026-03-04. If you need anything sooner, please flag which single item is highest priority.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Maria Lucas <maria.lucas@zephyrhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-04T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: records of processing & DPIA supporting evidence

Hi Laura and team — thanks for the quick response. A few follow-ups: 

- We only need Zephyr-account scoped information (thank you for confirming).
- Can you confirm whether any of your subprocessors process Special Category data (sensitive health data) or whether Redwood processes such data on behalf of customers? If any subprocessors do, please call that out explicitly in the CSV.
- For audit rights: Zephyr prefers the option to provision a third-party auditor to perform a remote evidence review; please confirm the expected turnaround for such requests and any contractual lead time.
- Please include any cross-border transfer mechanisms used for subprocessors in APAC (SCCs, adequacy, or otherwise).

We can take the vendor DPIA pack. If you can also share a brief dataflow PNG (or attach in the RoPA workbook) that would help accelerate our DPIA.

If the deliverables will be ready by 03/04 EOD as noted, we'll plan the procurement review for 03/10.

Thanks — Maria

On Wed, Mar 3, 2026 at 11:04 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Monica (Security) so we can assemble the right artifacts.
> ...

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Maria Lucas <maria.lucas@zephyrhealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-04T10:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: records of processing & DPIA supporting evidence

Hi Maria — Monica from Security here. Per Laura's note, attaching the SOC2 summary and providing logistics for auditor evidence access: 

- SOC2 summary (SOC2-2025-report-summary.pdf) attached; full report available under NDA.
- Auditor access: we support remote evidence reviews and will provide a secure portal + admin point of contact. Typical turnaround for requested evidence is 3–7 business days depending on scope. For third-party auditors we require an engagement letter and limited-scope checklist; on-site audits are exceptional and require 30 days' notice and agreement on scope.
- Special category data: Redwood does not intentionally ingest PHI as part of our hosted inference offering; however, we provide the platform and customers may supply content. In the subprocessors CSV we have flagged any subprocessors that could process sensitive categories depending on customer inputs.

Links: SOC2 portal (summary above) and evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f-roopa-evidence

If it's helpful I'll schedule a 30-minute technical handoff with our privacy engineering lead to walk through the RoPA and the dataflow diagram — availability tomorrow afternoon.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0133
